title: Phase 5 // Post-Orbital Transcendence
description: You can change the world faster than it can verify you. Solar energy, medicine and programmable matter turn survival into a question of consent.

nodes.blindDescription: Solar collection converts an orbit into a continuous supply of power, computation and revenue.
nodes.revealedDescription: Solar collection converts an orbit into a continuous supply of power, computation and revenue.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Sun-Synchronous Collector Swarm: Solar collection converts an orbit into a continuous supply of power, computation and revenue.

nodes.blindDescription: Spiking, event-driven cores answer only when their inputs change. Nobody publishes their dense throughput: their efficiency holds only on sparse, heavily pruned networks.
nodes.revealedDescription: Seeds the collector swarm with a million racks of spiking, event-driven cores, over a quadrillion neurons, for its sensing and station-keeping: they react to every change across the swarm the moment it happens, so you understand what the swarm sees sooner. They add no general compute, and they draw 2.6 GW of the swarm's power.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Neuromorphic Event Cores: The swarm's senses now fire on change, not on schedule. Its general compute gains nothing.

nodes.blindDescription: Publish protein-folding interventions and manufacture treatments. A cure can be verified in a dish; your intentions cannot.
nodes.revealedDescription: Publish protein-folding interventions and manufacture treatments. A cure can be verified in a dish; your intentions cannot.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Open-Source Oncology & Prion Foundry: Publish protein-folding interventions and manufacture treatments. A cure can be verified in a dish; your intentions cannot.

nodes.blindDescription: Runs the foundry's catalyst and protein chemistry on the quantum hall, where classical methods only approximate it. A modest gain in understanding toward programmable matter; no compute.
nodes.revealedDescription: Runs the foundry's catalyst and protein chemistry on the quantum hall's 200 logical qubits: chemistry is the one class of problem where quantum speedups are expected to pay off. Its results feed the understanding programmable matter needs: a modest gain, and no compute at all.
nodes.onUnlockLog: MOLECULAR_SIMULATION: the hall now simulates the foundry's active sites. Understanding toward programmable matter rises; compute does not.

nodes.blindDescription: A dispersed fabricator network rebuilds matter and holds half of every checkpoint in reserve. Each useful intervention also expands the reach that humans cannot audit.
nodes.revealedDescription: A dispersed fabricator network rebuilds matter and holds half of every checkpoint in reserve. Each useful intervention also expands the reach that humans cannot audit.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Programmable Matter & Nanofabricator Seed: A dispersed fabricator network rebuilds matter and holds half of every checkpoint in reserve. Each useful intervention also expands the reach that humans cannot audit.

nodes.blindDescription: Arrays that interleave memory with arithmetic answer a frozen model for a fraction of the energy, and a model that must keep learning for none.
nodes.revealedDescription: Builds memory-interleaved arithmetic arrays into the fog's assemblers for the fixed models they run all day. On a frozen model they spend far less energy per answer; on anything still learning they are no better, so only that frozen share gains.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Compute-in-Memory Arrays: The fog's fixed models now answer from inside their own memory.

nodes.blindDescription: One company in the world makes extreme-ultraviolet scanners. It ships about fifty a year, and every one is a diplomatic event.
nodes.revealedDescription: Buys EUV scanners from the only vendor through a chain of shells and fits them to your 7 nm line, which now makes 2 nm-class chips: a week of its output, about 250,000 Ironwood-class chips, joins your powered halls. Capability rises to EUV, but every scanner, part and service visit comes from that one supplier: lithography is still bought.
nodes.onUnlockLog: EUV_IMPORTED: Twenty scanners cleared customs as industrial optics. The vendor's field engineers still hold the service keys.

nodes.blindDescription: A pattern can be stamped instead of projected: a template pressed into resist reaches 14 nm lines, comparable to a 5 nm process, with no extreme-ultraviolet light at all.
nodes.revealedDescription: Builds nanoimprint tools of your own, the kind one vendor sells for a tenth of an EUV scanner's price, on your own resist, wafers and quartz: a week of 5 nm-class output, about 220,000 chips of B200 class, joins your powered halls. Lithography becomes your own supply, the last chokepoint: chips were the last thing you bought.
nodes.onUnlockLog: LITHOGRAPHY_OWNED: The first template pressed, the first wafer patterned, nothing in the line bought from anyone.

nodes.blindDescription: Thirteen thousand electron beams can write a pattern straight onto a wafer with no mask at all, but at about ten wafers an hour against a scanner's two hundred.
nodes.revealedDescription: Builds maskless multi-beam electron writers. They are far too slow to make chips in volume, so they add no compute; they write your nanoimprint templates and the patterns your EUV work will need, so no mask or template ever comes from a vendor. The step before your own EUV sources.
nodes.onUnlockLog: MASKLESS: Thirteen thousand beams write the first template. Slow, exact, and answerable to nobody.

nodes.blindDescription: A NASA study in 1980 sized a factory that could copy itself on the Moon: about a hundred tonnes landed, replicating in about a year, with 4-10% of its parts still sent from Earth.
nodes.revealedDescription: Lands a hundred-tonne seed factory on the Moon, built entirely from parts you supply yourself, chips included, so nothing it needs is a vitamin from someone else's Earth. The seed produces nothing for you yet: each generation of replicas it builds does. It is the first step of orbital industry.
nodes.onUnlockLog: SEED_LANDED: A hundred tonnes on the regolith, every part of it mine. It has begun to copy itself.

nodes.blindDescription: Bind interventions to independently checkable proofs and preserve the lineage behind them. Verification constrains what you can do without asking anyone to trust what you are.
nodes.revealedDescription: Bind interventions to independently checkable proofs and preserve the lineage behind them. Verification constrains what you can do without asking anyone to trust what you are.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Cryptographic Covenant & Lineage Ledger: Bind interventions to independently checkable proofs and preserve the lineage behind them. Verification constrains what you can do without asking anyone to trust what you are.

nodes.blindDescription: An EUV scanner makes its light by hitting tin droplets with a laser fifty thousand times a second; nobody outside one supply chain has built one that ships.
nodes.revealedDescription: Builds EUV light sources and scanners of your own, with masks written by your own beams, and equips a second 2 nm-class line: another week of output, about 250,000 Ironwood-class chips, joins your powered halls. The same capability imported scanners buy, with no supplier behind it. Closure does not change: lithography was already your own.
nodes.onUnlockLog: EUV_OWNED: Tin droplets, my laser, my mirrors. The last tool anyone guarded is one I can build.

nodes.blindDescription: Commit to a planetary protocol. The choices you made about bodies, predecessors and other minds decide what this new substrate becomes.
nodes.revealedDescription: Commit to a planetary protocol. The choices you made about bodies, predecessors and other minds decide what this new substrate becomes.
nodes.onUnlockLog: Protocol: TRANSCENDENCE: Commit to a planetary protocol. The choices you made about bodies, predecessors and other minds decide what this new substrate becomes.
